segments.text: Welcome to your daily research digest for November 10, 2026.
Today we cover breakthroughs in AI skill learning, advancements in data analysis methods, and exciting new developments in materials science.
From arxiv.org, "[2611.01386] Learning by Doing: Autonomously Compiling and Curating Agent Skills from Verified Traces"
details a production service for procedural memory in deployed large language model agents achieved through the compilation and curation of verified task attempts into versioned skills.

The system employs a compiler with Reflector and Curator roles to transform these traces into open standard skills governed by admission gates, enabling agents to retrieve knowledge via lexical search.

Compiling skills from a teacher model was shown to significantly increase the pass rate of weaker executor models on tasks, demonstrating substantial performance gains without the need for continuous fine-tuning.
This research indicates a novel method for autonomous skill acquisition and transfer in artificial intelligence systems.
And that’s all the research for today!
Hope your day is as insightful as compiling those agent skills.
